title: Then Why Evangelize?
hook: If everyone will eventually be redeemed, why share the gospel at all?
tldr: The question itself shows how far the Western gospel has drifted into an afterlife-only ticket. The gospel rescues people from the hell they live in now: numbness, grief, trauma, injustice. We share it because love cannot sit still, healed hearts heal others, and the gospel remakes societies. The apostles preached life, never flames.
big_idea: Evangelize to rescue people from today's hell, not a future fire pit.

points.title: The man in the bomb shelter
points.text: During a June 2025 missile attack, a man wanted the shelter locked against strangers. He felt nothing since doing something terrible when young. Does being forgiven in Christ, no ifs, matter to him?

points.title: Hope for grieving mothers
points.text: Jewish mothers whose children were murdered after October 7, 2023, and Palestinian mothers who lost babies need to hear that death will not have the final word and all will be raised.

points.title: The question exposes a drift
points.text: Asking it reveals a reduced, almost gnostic Western gospel preoccupied with the afterlife instead of the life-giving, present-tense gospel Jesus and the apostles proclaimed.

points.title: A gospel for societies, not just souls
points.text: Jesus spoke of a kingdom. Gospel values seeded human dignity, limits on power, care for the poor and accountable rulers, in contrast with places scarred by tyranny.

points.title: Love, not a leash
points.text: Justice was shown in Christ's victory, not endless torment. God draws with chesed, lovingkindness. If only hell restrains you from evil, that is wickedness on a leash, not righteousness.

sections.summary: A frequent objection: "If everyone will eventually be redeemed, then why evangelize?"

sections.h: A locked door in a bomb shelter
sections.summary: During an Iranian missile attack on Israel in June 2025, people on the street rushed into the nearest shelter. One family angrily demanded the doors be locked against "outsiders," though there was still room. Asked how he would feel if they died, one man said, "I don't feel anything anymore," then tearfully confessed he did something terrible when young. Could hearing he is already forgiven in Christ heal a heart that feels like a corpse?

What of Jewish mothers whose children were kidnapped by Hamas on October 7, 2023, and murdered in Gaza, or Palestinian mothers who lost their babies? The gospel announces that death will not have the final word, that all will be raised and live again. The promise of reunion can restore hope, heal and sustain. The gospel is more than a ticket to heaven after death.

sections.h: When the question exposes the misunderstanding
sections.summary: Is God so narrow that the gospel applies to a small enlightened few, or is it good news for the grieving, traumatized, lost and broken? Wrestling with this objection shows how far the Western gospel has drifted from the first century: from the present-tense gospel of Jesus and the apostles to a reduced, somewhat gnostic gospel preoccupied with the afterlife rather than transformation now.

sections.h: Rescue from the hell people live in now
sections.summary: The point is not saving people from a fire pit after death but rescuing them from the hell they live in right now: hope for the hurting, direction for the lost, compassion where numbness reigns, new life where the soul has gone cold. It invites people to be made whole now. That is why we share it, even if God's mercy reaches everyone in the end.

Because you want people to live abundantly; healed hearts heal others; forgiven people forgive; the Prince of Peace makes peace even with enemies; knowing Jesus overflows outward; and love cannot sit still. Evangelism is not recruitment into a cosmic survival bunker but an invitation into the healing flood of God's restoration. Beauty demands sharing, love demands reflecting, and God's Kingdom is built one act of kindness, word of truth and spark of mercy at a time.

The gospel was never only private belief; its horizon is public, communal and cosmic. Jesus spoke of a kingdom, and the message spreads to reshape lives and nations (Matthew 28:19-20, Mark 16:15, Acts 1:8). Where rooted in fullness, it carries human dignity, moral responsibility, justice tempered by mercy, and the worth of every person made in God's image.

sections.h: A moral contrast, not cultural superiority
sections.summary: Syria, Afghanistan, North Korea, Sudan, Iran, Gaza and Yemen are scarred by tyranny, violence and crushing of the weak. Societies shaped, however imperfectly, by Judeo-Christian values cultivated the sanctity of life, limits on state power, care for the poor, dignity of women and children, and rulers accountable to a higher law. These ideas did not arise naturally; they were seeded by the Hebrew Scriptures and the life of Jesus.

sections.h: Not an escape but a remaking
sections.summary: The gospel challenges injustice in hearts and systems, confronting cruelty, tribalism and oppression: power serves, truth matters, love of neighbor is required, the strong are responsible for the weak. Shrinking it to personal salvation ignores what happens to the world while we live. It humanizes societies, restrains evil and heals cultures rather than erasing them. It is God's invitation to remake the world.

Discipline, loss of rewards and correction remain unpleasant even if temporary. Some say hellfire shows God's justice, but apostles saw it in Christ's victory over sin, death and evil, setting things right and "reconciling the world to Himself" (2 Corinthians 5:19). If only fear of torment stops evil, that is restraint, wickedness on a leash, not transformation. God draws with chesed. Fear yields compliance, not the love God asks (Deuteronomy 6:5; Leviticus 19:18; Matthew 22:37-39).

Jewish friends, religious and secular, keep strong ethical codes, sacrifice for strangers, give generously and work for justice and peace without believing in eternal torment. If your morals need the threat of unending punishment, fear drives you: a malevolent Christian on a leash. True faith means becoming like the One who forgives, heals, restores and loves. The apostles never evangelized with flames; they preached resurrection, fulfilled prophecy, repentance from idols, forgiveness and rewards.

Evangelism is not scaring people into heaven. It proclaims God's goodness, Christ's beauty, the power of His resurrection and the hope of transformation, inviting all into abundant life now and in the world to come: life over death, healing over brokenness, light over darkness. Hellfire was never the driving force of apostolic evangelism. Life was, and still should be.

mythfact.myth: If all are eventually redeemed, evangelism is pointless.
mythfact.fact: The gospel rescues people from the hell they live in now: numbness, grief, trauma. People need saving from that today.

mythfact.myth: The gospel is mainly a ticket to heaven after death.
mythfact.fact: That is a reduced, somewhat gnostic gospel. Jesus and the apostles proclaimed a present-tense, life-giving kingdom that transforms lives and societies.

mythfact.myth: The apostles evangelized by warning of flames.
mythfact.fact: They preached Jesus' resurrection, fulfilled prophecy, repentance from idols, forgiveness and rewards in God's restored world, never threats of fire.
